verdict.rationale: Plaid documents self-serve API keys obtained by signing up in the Dashboard, a cloneable Quickstart app, and a free Sandbox where test Items can be created through Link or the `/sandbox/public_token/create` endpoint. Client-library evidence is limited to the Node library (plaid-node), so the 'in my language' part of the story is only partly shown. missing for 10: evidence of official client libraries across multiple languages, independent or hands-on confirmation that signup-to-first-sandbox-link is actually fast.

support.subject: As a developer, I can go from signup to my first linked sandbox account fast — self-serve API keys, a runnable quickstart, and client libraries in my language

citations.quote: Let's test out running Plaid locally by cloning the Quickstart app. You'll need API keys, which you can receive by signing up in the Dashboard.
The Plaid Sandbox is a free and fully-featured environment for application development and testing... you can create an unlimited number of test Items.
you can also create Items in Sandbox via the API, using a special Sandbox-only endpoint, /sandbox/public_token/create.
All errors can now be caught using try/catch with async/await or through promise chaining.
